overview: This House resolution directs the House Ethics Committee and the Office of Congressional Workplace Rights, which handles workplace complaints in Congress, to make certain records public within 60 days. They must release a list naming each member of the House who was the subject of a review or investigation into sexual harassment or sexual abuse that led to a payment of taxpayer money, along with the total amount paid in each member's case. They must also publish overall totals for taxpayer-funded settlements involving members that did not involve sexual misconduct, and separate totals for cases involving House employees, with and without sexual misconduct. Any settlement is counted as involving sexual misconduct if that was any part of the case, even if it was classified under another category. The House adopted it on June 30, 2026.
for: Supporters say taxpayers deserve to know when public money has been used to settle harassment claims against lawmakers, and that public disclosure promotes accountability and deters misconduct.
against: Critics say naming members tied to settlements, regardless of the outcome of the investigation, could harm reputations without a finding of wrongdoing and could discourage victims who wanted their cases kept confidential.
